study_identification_part.si4_title: A normative modelling approach reveals age-atypical cortical thickness in a subgroup of males with autism spectrum disorder

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Parameterize cortical thickness (CT) as individualized age-normed deviation (w-scores) to identify ASD subgroups with atypical CT and assess associations with behavioral symptomatology, contrasting against traditional case–control analyses.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: Participants were drawn from ABIDE I and II across multiple sites.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: we utilized the ABIDE datasets (ABIDE I and II)... Across both ABIDE I and ABIDE II CT was extracted...

rci2_hc_n.reason: 本研究では皮質厚（CT）の規範モデリングを実施するために、当初、広範な年齢層（5歳から40歳）をカバーする大規模サンプル（各グループN=870）が使用されました。性差やデータ量の制約から、実際の規範モデリングは男性のみのデータを用いて行われました。

rci3_hc_age.reason:
規範モデリングは男性のみのデータを用いて実施されました。
当初、健常者（TD）の初期データセットには、男性660名に加えて女性210名の情報が含まれていましたが、女性のデータは規範モデリングの構築からは除外されました。
女性のデータが除外された主な理由は以下の通りです。
1. 性差のある発達軌道（Sex differential developmental trajectories）: 女性と男性の間で発達の軌道が異なることが知られており、皮質厚（CT）の性差も報告されているためです。
2. 利用可能なデータの不足 (Lack of available data): 女性グループのサンプルサイズが小さく、特に年齢別ビンに分割した場合に、人口規範（population norms）を推定するのに十分なデータポイントを確保できなかったためです。
このため、最終的に規範モデリング（年齢に関連する皮質厚の変動）は、TDグループの男性のみのデータ（「Methods」セクションで詳細に説明されているサンプル）を利用して行われました

rci8_quality_checking.detail: Euler number-based QC; excluded subjects with Euler ≥ ~300 (top 10%); re-matched samples; included Euler and in-scanner head motion (framewise displacement) as covariates in analyses; sensitivity analyses by iteratively excluding top motion/Euler subjects showed high spatial consistency.
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: We excluded all subjects with a Euler score of 300 or higher... included both Euler index and framewise displacement as confound variables... cross-validation by systematically excluding the top 5% of motion and top 5% of Euler subjects... resulting maps were highly consistent.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Included site as a fixed covariate in LME during case–control analyses; recognized large site effects on variance. Normative LOESS model trained on pooled TD males without explicit site harmonization.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: linear mixed effect modelling including site... A post-hoc collection of sites... scanners, acquisition sequences... highly heterogeneous. As a result, we observed that site had a large effect on explaining variance in CT.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Linear mixed effects for case–control (covariates: site, sex, age, in-scanner motion, Euler); Spearman correlations between regional w-scores and ADOS/SRS with FDR correction; sensitivity analyses excluding high motion/Euler subjects.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Normative modelling reveals that only a small subset of ASD individuals show highly age-atypical CT; removing these outliers reduces small case–control differences, and w-scores associate with ADOS/SRS in distinct cortical regions.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Matched samples (ASD n=870; TD n=870; age 5–40y). Conventional LME found 27/308 ROI differences (mostly |d|<0.2); excluding regional outlier patients (|w|>2) reduced significant regions to 14 (1.9× decrease). A small subset (n=14) showed global atypicality (global ratio>0.5), largely reflecting globally thinner cortex and likely QC-related effects. Regional w-scores correlated with SRS (lateral frontal/parietal) and ADOS (lateral/inferior temporal) after FDR correction. Sensitivity analyses indicated stability against motion/Euler exclusions; centile-based deviation correlated strongly with LOESS-based ratios.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Approach supports individualized deviation mapping and subgroup stratification; code and data available via GitHub; additional analyses extended to volume, surface area, and LGI in supplements.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Cross-sectional design limits trajectory inference; substantial site/scanner heterogeneity with large site effects; normative model restricted to males; LOESS may be sensitive to sparse age bins.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Two parcellations used (308 ROI Desikan–Killiany sub-parcellation; 360 HCP-MMP) with highly consistent patterns. Framewise displacement from resting-state fMRI computed to index motion and included as covariate. FreeSurfer recon-all steps detailed; failed reconstructions excluded prior to matching.
